title: The Watch Hut
logline: A farmer spends the night in a hut on stilts at the edge of a field, listening for the animals that come to eat what the season took months to grow.

object.note: Object 3 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a rival on the water to a threat that comes out of the dark: the question of what wanting turns into when something stands in the way follows a farmer up into a watch hut for the night.

thread_out.thread: The night's watch ends at dawn; on a southern beach another dawn's work, a hauled net, is divided into shares, and each division is a quick test of what is held back.

requirements: A farmer who genuinely keeps a night watch against crop-raiding animals during the filming window
Safe, agreed camera positions that do not increase risk to the farmer, crew or wildlife
Local guidance on the specific animals and current human-wildlife conflict conditions

suggestions.name: Chena and paddy farmland on the edge of dry-zone jungle
suggestions.region: Anuradhapura or Polonnaruwa district, North Central Province
suggestions.why: Well-known dry-zone farming districts bordering forest and scrub where crop-raiding by wild animals is a recognised part of the agricultural year.
suggestions.season_notes: Likely tied to the growing and ripening season of the specific crop.
suggestions.verify: A specific farmer, field and current wildlife activity must be confirmed with appropriate local and wildlife authority guidance.
